value.rationale: The best direction for a single Steiner inertia descent is a canonical natural geometric optimization; for a square its four slopes are unexpectedly oblique, and the exact achievable fractional contraction 1/27 is a sharp one-step quantitative benchmark. The complete rectangle profile adds generality and a geometric two-regime boundary, not just a computed isolated number. Iterative and universal-body extensions are not claimed.
